newsitem.title: USA: Stocks, bonds, rise; dollar surges against mark.
newsitem.headline: Stocks, bonds, rise; dollar surges against mark.

text.p: Stocks sailed to record highs for the third time this week and bond prices rallied Thursday as investors welcomed the latest signs of a slow-growth economy without much inflation.
The dollar surged against the German mark after Russian President Boris Yeltsin, in a surprise move, dismissed security chief Alexander Lebed.
Oil prices rose and gold ended little changed.
The Dow Jones industrial average rose 38.39 points to 6,059.20, surpassing Wednesday's record close of 6,020.81. It was the index's third high for the week and 30th this year.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,406 to 944 on heavy volume of 478 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

"We're seeing for the most part a continuation of a favourable interpretation of earnings news coming out and today's economic reports support the thesis the economy is growing at a rate even Goldilocks cannot quibble with -- not too hot or too cold," said Jim Solloway, director of research at Argus Research.
Other market measures also hit new highs. The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 2.58 to 706.99 -- its third record close for the week.
But the Nasdaq composite index fell for a second day, losing 9.03 points to 1,241.96.

The latest economic data lessened the odds that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates any time soon, analysts said. Higher rates would tend to draw funds away from stocks and into money market accounts, CDs, and other interest-bearing investments.
New-home building slumped and industrial production grew at a slower rate in September while stocks of unsold goods rose in August, separate government reports said.

In the Treasury market, the 30-year Treasury bond rose three-quarters of a point, lowering its yield, which moves in the opposite direction from the price, to 6.80 percent from 6.86 percent late Wednesday.
Ironically the stock market's gains came as the ninth anniversary of Black Monday looms. On Oct. 19, 1987, the Dow plummeted 508.00 points or 22.61 percent, the biggest crash ever.
Analysts said the big difference between now and 1987 was that interest rates were then at 10 percent and rising, while they are now steady and below 7 percent.
"I was scared in October 1987 and a bit concerned in October 1989 but these were Octobers where the market was out of sync with fundamentals," said Solloway.

In currency markets, the dollar rallied against the mark after Yeltsin unexpectedly dismissed the charismatic Lebed, in office only four months, in a speech on national television. Yeltsin cited Lebed's lack of team spirit and obvious ambition to become Russia's next leader.
The dollar immediately jumped to 1.5454 marks, its highest level since May, on the news. It later settled a bit to close at 1.5427, up from 1.5400 in late trade Wednesday.
"The knee-jerk reaction was people see more instability in Russia so they sold the mark," said David Solin, partner at Foreign Exchange Analytics.

The mark typically falls on political instability in Russia given Germany's geographical proximity and economic links with the country. The dollar also is seen as a safe haven during political unrest, as is the Swiss franc.
The dollar fell slightly against the Japanese yen to 112.19 yen from 112.30 yen late on Wednesday despite strong buying interest from Japan, dealers said.

Oil prices ended higher with traders awaiting Friday's meeting between Energy Secretary Hazel O'Leary and oil industry executives to discuss possible ways to curb heating oil price spikes this winter.

At the New York Mercantile Exchange, November crude oil ended 25 cents higher at $25.42 a barrel, November heating oil rose 0.73 cent to close at 72.29 cents a gallon and November unleaded gasoline rose 1.08 cents a gallon to 66.53 cents.
December gold fell 40 cents to $382.60 an ounce in New York trading.
Overseas, London's FTSE 100 index rose 17.7 points to 4,042.1. Tokyo's 225-share Nikkei average edged up 26.55 points to 21,423.74.
